10 Apr 2017 · Paper · Nature Neuroscience 20, 872-878

The neural correlates of dreaming

Siclari F, Baird B, Perogamvros L, Bernardi G, LaRocque JJ, Riedner B, Boly M, Postle BR, Tononi G

Less slow activity at the back of the brain marked dreaming in both kinds of sleep, and could predict a dream report in real time.

People were woken many times a night and asked if they had been dreaming. In both dreaming-heavy and dreaming-light stages of sleep, a dream report followed a drop in slow brain waves over a 'hot zone' at the back of the head. Watching that zone live predicted whether the sleeper would report a dream.

High-density EEG, serial awakenings. Dream reports in NREM and REM associated with local decreases in low-frequency activity in posterior cortex; high-frequency activity there correlated with specific dream contents; real-time monitoring predicted dream vs no-dream reports in NREM.

What we do with it

The sharpest within-stage test of a measure against report. The DREAM database (2025) lets us test whether it replicates across labs. Planned
